newsitem.title: USA: Bush to fulfill pledge with parachute jump.
newsitem.headline: Bush to fulfill pledge with parachute jump.

text.p: Former President George Bush, 72, plans to make a parachute jump on Tuesday to fulfil a pledge he made to himself after his Navy plane was shot down in World War Two, a U.S. Army spokesman said on Monday.

Bush, who made his first parachute jump out of a crippled airplane over the Pacific Ocean during the war, will jump from a civilian aircraft about 12,000 feet (3,658 metres) over Yuma Proving Ground in Arizona, a Bush spokesman said.

"According to President Bush's people, President Bush made a promise when he bailed out of his plane in World War Two in the Pacific that someday he would make a parachute jump out of an airplane that wasn't an emergency jump," Army spokesman Doug Smith said.
Bush renewed that pledge at a recent meeting of the U.S. Parachute Association where he was given a vintage World War Two parachute.

A member of the parachute association and two military experts from the Army's Golden Knights parachute team will join Bush on the jump, which was scheduled for 12:30 p.m. EST (1730 GMT), Bush spokesman Jim McGrath said.
Bush will jump out of the plane attached to a safety harness held by two of the parachutists, then be released to make the freefall solo after his parachute deploys, he said.
"They say it's just like stepping off a curb," McGrath said. "Once he's OK, they'll signal to each other somehow and let him go solo."
Bush, accompanied by his wife Barbara, was in Yuma on Monday afternoon training with the Army experts, he said.
